LOOK: “Tay, Kami Naman!” Signature Drive is in Davao City.

Supporters of former President Rodrigo Roa Duterte launched a signature campaign titled “Tay, Kami Naman!” on Monday, January 12, at Rizal Park on San Pedro Street here. 

The activity, which started earlier today, gathered hundreds of participants who affixed their signatures to express support for the initiative. Organizers said the signature drive will run until 7:00 p.m.

Davao residents and park visitors still have hours left to express their support. The event drew steady foot traffic as volunteers facilitated the signing process at designated areas within the park. via Ivy Tejano | MB

data.text:
President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Friday made his second visit to San Francisco High School (SFHS) in Bago Bantay, Quezon City, to inspect the ongoing reconstruction of the school building that was damaged by fire last June 15.

President Marcos also oversaw the Yaman ng Kalusugan Program Para Malayo sa Sakit (YAKAP) at the Kalinga medical caravan of the Department of Education (DepEd) and the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) being held on campus.

The President first visited the school on June 18 last year, just three days after a fire had razed the two-storey, 10-classroom DAO building that had been in use for over 45 years.

During that visit, President Marcos ordered the construction of a new four-storey building with 36 classrooms, significantly upgrading the destroyed facility.

The new school building being constructed by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is expected to be completed by the start of the next school year, the President said during the inspection on Friday.

The President also said he asked SM Group to build 24 classrooms for the school.

According to DepEd, SFHS has 6,846 students supported by 325 teaching and non-teaching personnel, and has 211 classrooms.

YAKAP is PhilHealth’s expanded Konsulta program for schools aimed at protecting the health and well-being of students and teachers as a foundation of quality education.

Doctors and medical personnel from the Quezon City Health Office conducted vision screenings and laboratory tests using the First Lady’s Lab for All Mobile Medical Van, which was donated to the Quezon City government.

Free medicines were also distributed to beneficiaries while PhilHealth conducted registration for new members.

The SFHS mission marked the first YAKAP Caravan in 2026, following similar caravans held in seven schools last year.
